sealed.statement: The ProjectionReadinessEvidenceOwner semantic generation for a node is scoped to that node's own semantic dependencies plus one GLOBAL readiness revision, so an authoritative mutation that cannot change node N's normalized semantic core does not rotate N's generation, while every mutation that can change it still does. The generation owner (projection-readiness-evidence-generation.js) classifies every field of the owner-path source S(N) = {dimensions, runtimeAuthority, priorityControlPlaneRecovery, runtimeServeEligible, nodeEvidence, membershipPublication} as CONTENT-covered (canonically digested per node; nodeEvidence joins this class with its two clock-derived ages classified as observation-time) or GLOBAL-VERSION-covered (membershipPublication via the synchronous CONTROL_PLANE_PUBLICATIONS mutation version, which is the global readiness revision); the five cluster-wide NODES/SERVICES/PARTITIONS/STORAGE_RESERVATIONS/REPLICA_OPERATIONS table versions leave the key because every route from those tables into the core passes through a digested verdict; the planning version key and the v2/v4 live semantic verdicts stay; the sync-path membership-publication diagnostics memo is keyed on the same global revision so a publication apply can never be observed stale under the new generation. Invariants: (DEP-SCOPE) every field reaching the owner seam is classified with a source-owner justification and the seam fails CLOSED (build without memoizing, counted) for any unclassified field, any digest depth overflow, or an unavailable global revision — a known-global dependency localized incorrectly must red; (A1) an authoritative mutation proven to affect only node A rotates A's generation and rebuilds A while B's generation is unchanged and B returns the SAME semantic-core reference without normalizing again; (A2) A observes the new semantic result — no stale node-local entry; (A3) a CONTROL_PLANE_PUBLICATIONS change rotates every node's generation; (A4) a mutation affecting a bounded node subset rebuilds exactly that subset while the rest reuse; (A5) live transport/lifecycle/publication-mode/repair changes rotate the generation exactly as established by v2 DEP and v4, and raw nodeEvidence transport fields now rotate it even without a boolean flip; (A6) an authoritative publication change arriving while a normalized graph is being built, or between a cache apply and its deferred listener on the sync path, never publishes old evidence under the new node/global generation, on the REAL SystemTableCache; (ENGAGEMENT) under production-shaped churn (5 nodes, writes repeatedly affecting one/some nodes, moving clock) unaffected nodes' semantic cores actually reuse, and the receipt reds when the six cluster-wide table versions are restored; (BOUNDED-WORK) builds(N) <= node-local generation changes affecting N + global generation changes + 1 initial build — never total cluster table writes x node count; the generation uses no TTL, clock, evaluation count or object identity. Scope owns ONLY the generation granularity of the ProjectionReadinessEvidenceOwner and the sync publication-diagnostics memo keying; it does NOT own OwnerKeyReconcileQueue cadence, ReadinessPlanningSnapshotOwner loop frequency, the 250ms planning latch, trust-state/dispatch caller frequency, candidate-derivation self-cost, storage_reservation_reconcile, or schema admission.

constraints.statement: If this Quest changes source code, spawn a subagent verifier before audit and git handoff, then record a Solver finding with evidence subagent:<id>.

claim: DEP-SCOPE verdict: locality is provable without per-table row-attribution rules. The owner-path seam source is exactly {dimensions, runtimeAuthority, priorityControlPlaneRecovery, runtimeServeEligible, nodeEvidence, membershipPublication} (pinned on sync+async paths); five of the six cluster-wide table versions (NODES/SERVICES/PARTITIONS/STORAGE_RESERVATIONS/REPLICA_OPERATIONS) only ever reached the core through digested verdicts and were the measured A3 over-invalidation; membershipPublication is GLOBAL by its owner's definition (cluster highest-epoch row) and keeps the CONTROL_PLANE_PUBLICATIONS mutation version as the global revision; nodeEvidence is node-local by construction (every input keyed by nodeId) and becomes its own content-digested node stamp with heartbeatAgeMs/readyLeaseAgeMs classified observation-time. Map: solve/evidence/projection-readiness-per-node-generation-granularity.dep-scope.md

Mechanism choice: content digests, not owner-bumped counters. A counter bumped from systemTableCache.onCacheChange would be UNSOUND: listeners fire on setImmediate (system-table-cache-observation-methods.js:267) while the mutation version bumps synchronously (system-table-cache.js:540), so a sync read between apply and listener would reuse a stale core for one macrotask. Content-digested segments cannot straddle (the key IS the observed content); the single version-covered field keeps the synchronous table version plus the R6 bracket. No source owner exposes readiness-specific counters.

Latent A6 hole closed in scope: the sync-path membershipPublicationDiagnosticsMemo was cleared only by the deferred cache listener, so a sync build between a publication apply and its listener observed STALE diagnostics under the NEW version and the owner memoized a stale core against it — masked in v3/v4 only because the five other cluster-wide versions rotated every key within ~50ms. The memo is now keyed on the same global revision (control-plane-readiness-publication-diagnostics.js readMembershipPublicationDiagnosticsRevision); receipt A6 drives the exact interleaving on the real SystemTableCache.

Out-of-scope owner finding (NOT fixed here): the CL-012 stored-snapshot reuse layer (control-plane-readiness-stored-snapshot-reuse.js getFresherStoredReadinessSnapshot) has the same deferred-listener window — between a CONTROL_PLANE_PUBLICATIONS apply and its listener it serves the stored projectionReadinessContract (old epoch) under a freshly overridden top-level membershipPublication (new epoch), an internally inconsistent snapshot for one macrotask. Its reuse gate compares the SERVICES version but not the publication version; a follow-up can key it on the same global revision. Separate owner (snapshot store, a readiness-freshness-macrotask-bound pair file), so left out of this quest by scope discipline.

Retained planning segment is provably redundant with the content digests: the planning snapshot reaches the core only through runtimeAuthority.recoveryEligible and priorityControlPlaneRecovery, both digested, so a planning tick that changes neither cannot change any core. It stays in the key per operator instruction as conservative cluster-wide invalidation (250ms wall-clock latch => <=4 rotations/s in production) and is the expected dominant residual rotator; the owner now attributes every build to the segment that rotated (stats().buildCountByCause + per-cause sync sections) so the GCP re-profile can read its share directly. Fixture caveat: the latch keys on Date.now() while test fixtures drive a fake service clock, so in fixtures the planning key rotates on every write; ENGAGEMENT therefore holds the segment constant and BOUNDED-WORK bounds it independently on the wall clock.

MEASURED (local docker 5-node formation, seed, like-for-like 5 windows): v1 candidate reuse 8.8% -> 14.5% only; per-cause build attribution shows node-local causes ~6% of builds while the two RETAINED cluster-wide segments account for 93% (global whole-table CONTROL_PLANE_PUBLICATIONS version 50.1%, planning derivation key 43.1%), each still rotating every node ~14-19/s. Semantically correct but nearly inert in production — the sealed global-segment mechanism (whole-table version) is falsified as insufficient. Evidence: solve/evidence/projection-readiness-per-node-generation-granularity.effectiveness-measurement.md

Planning latch flaps in production (separate owner, explicit non-scope): readMembershipPlanningDerivationVersionKey is fed ISO observedAt strings by the readiness service (Date.now fallback) and NUMERIC pass-start observedAt values by the rebalancer (unified-rebalancer-priority-readiness.js:472,379); a refresh with an older now moves refreshedAtMs backwards, so the 250ms latch does not hold (~14 rotations/s/node observed vs 4/s bound). Every consumer of the key (planning-snapshot memo, candidate-derivation memo, placement-observation memo, readiness key) misses at that rate — a candidate cause for the parked candidate-derivation self-cost owner.

Joiner fail-closed engagement: node-2/node-4 logged 704/864 owner_unowned_build_global_revision_unavailable during their join window (cache without a version surface). v3/v4 memoized that window on a constant token with membershipPublication UNCOVERED (latent joiner under-invalidation); v2's content coverage needs no version surface.

Ruled out for the successor: per-table row-attribution counters bumped from onCacheChange (deferred listener, unsound; DEP-SCOPE finding 2); the whole-table CONTROL_PLANE_PUBLICATIONS version as the global segment (measured 50% of residual builds; rotates on every publication-table write incl. refreshes/acks/timestamps that leave the membership diagnostics' semantic content unchanged); retaining the planning derivation key in the readiness key (measured 43% of residual builds; provably redundant with the digested verdicts).

note: Measurement falsified the sealed global-segment mechanism: the whole-table publication version and the retained planning segment are 93% of residual builds; the lever is full content coverage of the key (digest membershipPublication with a per-frozen-object digest cache; no cluster-wide version segment; planning segment out as provably redundant). Reseal as v2.

reason: Sealed mechanism for the global segment (whole-table CONTROL_PLANE_PUBLICATIONS version) and the retained planning segment measured as 93% of residual builds (reuse 8.8%->14.5% only); successor v2 seals a fully content-covered generation. Evidence: solve/evidence/projection-readiness-per-node-generation-granularity.effectiveness-measurement.md
